newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANZ climbs to record high after profit.
newsitem.headline: ANZ climbs to record high after profit.

text.p: Shares in Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ) edged to a record high on Wednesday afternoon after the release of its half year results.
At 2.05 p.m (0405 GMT), ANZ shares were 11 cents higher at A$8.68, after earlier hitting a record high of A$8.70, which breached its previous record of A$8.644, set on February 19.
ANZ shares were trading 14 cents lower at A$8.56 before the results were released around 0255 GMT.
"The dividend was a cent better than the market expected and that has been reflected in the price," said a Melbourne broker.
ANZ reported an 18 percent rise in first half net profit to A$615 million and lifted its interim dividend 22 cents per share from 18 cents a year ago.
Analsyst had been forecasting a net profit of between A$580 million and A$630 million and a dividend of between 19 cents to 24 cents.
"It's good to see the market react positively to the result even though it is within the expectation range," said Scott Healy, a dealer at Brisbane broker, Wilson HTM.
Healy said the stock could soften over the afternoon if investors made the assessment that a fall in the doubtful debts charge was just a temporary boost to the bank's earnings.
The bank said its provision for doubtful debts fell to A$75 million in the half compared to A$102 million in the previous corresponding period.
